Subject: Exploring a move to annual prepay — high level asks

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're evaluating switching our Redwood billing from monthly to an annual prepay for 2027 to get better unit economics and simpler procurement. Before we pull Finance in, could you share: 1) a short playbook for conversion (discount ranges you typically offer for first-year prepay vs multi-year), 2) suggested ramp schedule (how you handle staged usage credits / true-up), and 3) any standard conditions (onboarding credits, termination clauses) you require?

Timeline: procurement needs a recommended term and payment schedule by week of Jul 6 — we have an internal board approver on Jul 15.

Also, please attach any example contract language or a sample pricing spreadsheet. We may loop Greg and our procurement team in on the follow-up.

Appreciate a quick sketch so we can align internally.

Best,
Aisha Khan
Sr. Procurement Manager
Nimbus Health

Hi Aisha —

Thanks for the clear ask. Quick sketch below and I attached a short summary PDF with options: prepay_options_summary_olga_v1.pdf. Happy to jump on a 30m call next week (I have Tue/Thu mornings PT).

Top-line options (all annual prepay, USD):
- 12mo prepay (single-year): ~18% list discount vs monthly effective rate; staged ramp true-up at month 4 and month 9; onboarding credit = $10k professional services credit.
- 24mo prepay (multi-year commit): ~23% year-1 effective discount with a 7% guaranteed renewal discount in year-2 if usage targets met; deferred invoice schedule possible.
- 36mo enterprise: custom pricing + capacity guarantee; requires finance review.

Ramp notes: we typically include a 3-step ramp: baseline (months 1–3) measured usage credit of up to 40% of committed baseline, progressive true-ups at month 4 (to confirm 50%) and month 9 (full). If actual usage exceeds committed, we bill the overage at agreed token rate on next invoice.

Conditions: standard prepay terms, DocuSign signature, 30–60 day payment window depending on credit profile, and a cap on cumulative onboarding concessions. I'll share an editable spreadsheet for modeling.

Olga

Subject: Fwd: Nimbus — convert monthly to annual prepay (need pricing recommendation)

Sergio / Marissa —

Aisha from Nimbus is asking for a recommendation and a playbook. They're conservative on cash but want simplicity — board sign-off mid-July. Proposed approach: 12mo prepay with an 18% effective discount and a $10k onboarding credit, or 24mo at 23% with a smaller up-front credit. Key questions: do we have authorization to offer the 23% multi-year at standard AE-levels, or do I need to route to revenue ops/finance?

Suggested commercial terms to propose to Nimbus (draft):
- 12-month prepaid commitment: 12-month invoice paid upfront net-30; 18% off list token rate; onboarding credit $10k (one-time).
- Ramp schedule: Month 1–3 allow up to 40% of committed tokens as usage credit (no charge), month 4 true-up invoice for 50% of committed, month 9 final true-up.
- Renewal: option to renew at published 12mo prepay rates less an incremental 5% loyalty credit if on-time payments and usage targets met.
- Clause: total concessions capped at $25k for year-1; any extra concessions require VP approval.

I've attached the pricing model workbook for modeling scenarios: pricing_model_nimbus.xlsx. Please review and call out any compliance or accounting concerns.

—Olga

Thanks Olga — good starting point. A few edits from sales ops perspective:
- Reduce year-1 discount to 16% for 12mo (keeps headroom for negotiating an onboarding credit) and keep 22% for 24mo.
- Offer a $7.5k onboarding credit (applies to PS hours only) unless they accept a 24mo where credit reduces to $5k.
- Propose a staged credit release tied to milestones: 50% of onboarding credit released at SOW sign, remainder at production launch. This avoids clawbacks.
- Add a clause: if usage is <60% of committed for first 120 days, customer may request a one-time credit extension; otherwise normal true-up applies.

Also recommend attaching the Ravello precedent for the finance reviewers — we got approval at 22% there for a 24mo. Loop Rishi for finance sign-off and keep concessions in the attached workbook.

Sergio

Subject: Redwood proposal — Nimbus Health prepaid conversion (12mo & 24mo options)

Hi Aisha / Greg,

Thanks for the quick turn. Per our internal review (cc'd Sergio and Marissa), please find our formal proposal below and attached as a PDF (nimbus_prepaid_proposal_20260718.pdf). High-level options: one-page summary first, detailed terms after.

Summary (USD, committed token-equivalent):
Option A — 12-month prepaid
- Committed: 150M tokens annual
- Price: $0.0092 per token (18% off monthly blended rate)
- Upfront invoice: $1,380,000 due net-30
- Onboarding credit: $10,000 (applies to PS only)
- Ramp: months 1–3 up to 40% of committed tokens are not charged; month 4 interim true-up invoice; month 9 final true-up.
- Concessions cap: $25,000 year-1

Option B — 24-month prepaid
- Year-1 committed: 125M tokens (volume-based)
- Price year-1: $0.0081 per token (23% effective discount)
- Year-2 renewal: published 12mo prepay less 7% if usage targets met
- Upfront invoice year-1: $1,012,500 due net-30; onboarding credit: $5,000

Commercial terms and contingencies:
- DocuSign MSA + SLA addendum required.
- 60-day invoice term can be provided on request pending finance approval.
- If actual usage < 60% of committed in first 120 days, customer may request a one-time extension; otherwise standard true-up applies.
- Total concessions in year-1 limited to agreed cap; any overages require VP sign-off.

Next steps:
1) Confirm preferred option (A or B) and preferred payment terms by Jul 22 so Legal & Finance can prepare final DocuSign.
2) If accepted, we'll generate a DocuSign envelope and SOW.
3) We will include SOC2 evidence and the standard redline-friendly MSA excerpt.

Links / attachments:
- Proposal PDF: nimbus_prepaid_proposal_20260718.pdf
- DocuSign (preview): https://docusign.com/envelope/ABC123-nimbus-prepay
- Modeling workbook (internal): https://drive.redwood.com/shared/nimbus/prepay-model

Happy to discuss on a quick call.

Respectfully,
